relationship-analytics.title: Relationship analytics overview – Dynamics 365 Sales – Microsoft Learn
relationship-analytics.notes: Relationship analytics in Dynamics 365 Sales takes the activity history between a seller and a contact or account and turns it into KPIs. Such KPIs exist for contacts, accounts, opportunities and leads, and they are shown graphically so sellers and sales managers can see which relationships need care and which indicators could improve. The basic tier is available out of the box and draws on emails and appointments sent and received in Dynamics 365, with widgets such as a summary, most contacted, customer interactions, email engagement and email sent/received ratio. The enhanced tier adds widgets like relationship health, hourly investment, similar won deals and response time. It requires a suitable Dynamics 365 Sales license plus an administrator who enables and configures relationship intelligence. Response time depends on a connection to Exchange Online, and similar won deals applies only to opportunities. Email engagement counts only emails that are tracked. The page also warns that the feature must not be used for decisions about employment, pay or similar employee rights, and customers remain responsible for lawful use.

relationship-intelligence.title: Relationship intelligence overview – Dynamics 365 Sales – Microsoft Learn
relationship-intelligence.notes: Relationship intelligence in Dynamics 365 Sales helps sales teams keep track of customer relationships by surfacing insight into relationship health, who knows whom and related topics. It is built on how salespeople interact with their customers, and its purpose is to monitor the health and risk of relationships and to spot customers that need attention. One component, relationship analytics and health, presents KPIs and activity trends for contacts, opportunities, leads and accounts, using interaction data from Dynamics 365 and Microsoft Exchange. It appears on opportunity forms, list views and charts. The second component, who knows whom, suggests colleagues who know a lead and lets the seller ask them by email for an introduction. This is based on email interactions and meetings in the organization's Exchange environment. Contacts or leads outside the Exchange organization can be queried, while internal users only in some cases. The page lists no licenses or prices and points to separate articles for configuring each component.

request-for-information-action.title: Request for information in agent flows – Microsoft Copilot Studio – Microsoft Learn
request-for-information-action.notes: The request for information action lets an agent flow pause, collect input from named human reviewers and use the answers in later steps. It is found under the human review category in the flow designer and needs a flow with a trigger that has been published before testing. The required fields are a title that becomes the email subject, a message with the request text, and an assigned-to list of recipients. When several recipients are listed, only the response of the first person to answer is processed. Inputs can be text, yes/no, email, number or date, and fields can be made optional and given placeholder text. Single-select and multi-select choices are possible only for text inputs. Each input produces a parameter that later actions, such as an AI approval, can use as dynamic content. Requests are currently sent only through Outlook and cannot go to users outside the tenant. A known issue is that outputs may be wrapped in double curly braces, which can be avoided by naming inputs without spaces. The page does not state licensing requirements.

restricted-content-discovery.title: Restricted content discovery – SharePoint in Microsoft 365 – Microsoft Learn
restricted-content-discovery.notes: Restricted content discovery is a site-level setting for SharePoint that limits how easily a site's content, including recently edited files, can be found through organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot answers. It is meant as a temporary governance control that buys time to review permissions while Copilot rollout continues. Admins turn it on in the SharePoint admin center or with the Set-SPOSite cmdlet, and affected sites show a restricted label. The setting also hides AI entry points on those sites, such as the Copilot button and creating pages with AI. Management can be delegated to site admins, who must then give a reason, and changes are recorded in the Microsoft Purview audit log. It requires a Microsoft Copilot license and SharePoint Advanced Management. It does not change permissions, does not remove content from the search index, and leaves eDiscovery and auto-labeling working. It applies to SharePoint sites only, not OneDrive. Typical targets are sites at risk of oversharing, such as finance or HR sites. Heavy use can reduce the completeness of search and Copilot results.

routing-diagnostics.title: View unified routing diagnostics – Dynamics 365 Customer Service – Microsoft Learn
routing-diagnostics.notes: Routing diagnostics in Dynamics 365 Customer Service gives a detailed view of each routed record so that problems in classifying and assigning work items can be investigated. Unified routing sends a work item to the most suitable service representative or queue based on skills and related entities. The diagnostics page lists columns such as work item, routing status, duration, work stream, queue, routed agent and rule hit policy. Each item is followed through the stages intake, classification, route to queue and assignment. Intake applies only to record routing, classification shows which rulesets and machine learning models ran, and assignment shows prioritization, the assignment method, capacity, presence, skills and an attempt trace. Admins switch it on from the routing area of the Copilot Service admin center, and data is kept in Dataverse. Routed records use more storage than other work item types, and information can appear with a delay. Some model details are marked as preview. The page states that the feature is deprecated and does not name specific license requirements.

runbook.title: Azure Automation runbook types – Microsoft Learn
runbook.notes: The page describes the runbook types in the process automation feature of Azure Automation rather than defining the term formally. The types are PowerShell, PowerShell Workflow, Python, Graphical and Graphical PowerShell Workflow. PowerShell and Python are the recommended text-based types, and the PowerShell runtime version is selected per runbook. Runbooks can run in Azure or on hybrid runbook workers, which can be Windows or Linux machines. Text runbooks can be edited in the portal or written offline and imported, while graphical runbooks can be edited only in the portal, although they can be exported and imported into other automation accounts. PowerShell Workflow adds checkpoints and parallel processing but must be compiled before running, so it starts more slowly and is not available on Linux hybrid workers. Python runbooks can use Python libraries, with modules supplied as wheel files, and do not support webhooks. Graphical runbooks cannot be converted to text types or digitally signed. Some PowerShell 7 limitations apply, such as no workflows and no signed runbooks. Runbooks can also call other runbooks as children, with restrictions across types.

saas-fulfillment-apis.title: SaaS fulfillment APIs – Partner Center – Microsoft Learn
saas-fulfillment-apis.notes: The SaaS fulfillment APIs let publishers, meaning independent software vendors, sell their software-as-a-service applications through Microsoft's commercial marketplace. They keep the subscription state on the publisher side in step with Microsoft and cover direct, partner-led and field-led sales channels. Integrating them is required before a transactable SaaS offer or a free trial can be created and published in Partner Center. The documented flows include the landing page flow that tells the publisher about a purchase, activation, optional automatic activation, updates to plan or license count, and suspend and reinstate when a payment method is invalid. Webhooks report changes and cancellations triggered on the Microsoft side. Cancellation integration is optional because customers can cancel there as well. Prerequisites are registering the application as a Microsoft Entra application and using service-to-service authentication, with calls made only from the publisher's backend and not from web pages. Version 2 is the recommended version, and version 1 is deprecated and no longer documented. For reseller purchases through a cloud solution provider, the publisher does not have to implement the flows differently.

saga-pattern.title: Saga design pattern – Azure Architecture Center – Microsoft Learn
saga-pattern.notes: The saga pattern keeps data consistent across several services by running a sequence of local transactions. Each service commits its own work in its own database and triggers the next step through an event or message. If a step fails, compensating transactions reverse the effects of the steps already completed. It serves as an alternative to two-phase commit in distributed systems where ACID guarantees do not span multiple databases. The page separates compensable transactions, a pivot transaction that marks the point of no return, and retryable transactions that follow it and must be idempotent. Sagas can be coordinated by choreography, where services exchange events without a central controller, or by orchestration, where a central orchestrator tracks task state and handles failures. Choreography is simple but can become hard to follow and risks cyclic dependencies, while orchestration suits complex workflows but adds coordination effort. Drawbacks include a different mental model, harder debugging, compensations that may themselves fail, and anomalies such as lost updates and dirty reads because sagas lack isolation. Countermeasures include semantic locks and versioning.

sales-qualification-agent.title: Configure the Sales Qualification Agent – Dynamics 365 Sales – Microsoft Learn
sales-qualification-agent.notes: The Sales Qualification Agent supports sellers with lead research, assessing how well a lead fits the target customer profile, and first email outreach. Admins describe the company, its products and the ideal customer so the agent matches the sales strategy. It runs in one of two modes per organization: research-only, which analyzes assigned leads, drafts outreach emails and recommends actions, or research and engage, which contacts customers autonomously and hands leads with buying interest to sellers based on configured handover criteria. Moving from research-only to research and engage is possible, but not the reverse. Setup covers lead selection criteria, email instructions, handoff criteria, assignment rules, knowledge sources and connected skills for suggested actions. Prerequisites include admin rights, a Copilot Studio license, modern UI for the Sales Hub app, suitable data policies and server-side synchronization with Exchange. The engage mode also needs an Azure app, an app user and a shared mailbox. A configured agent cannot be deleted without Microsoft Support, and stopping it only prevents new lead assignments.

saml.title: SAML vs OIDC decision guide – Microsoft Entra – Microsoft Learn
saml.notes: In this Microsoft Entra decision guide, SAML 2.0 is described as a mature, XML-based federation protocol that enterprises have used widely for a long time. Its purpose is to share sign-in and access information securely between identity providers and applications. Identity data travels in XML messages called assertions, which can carry detailed user attributes and support signed assertions and complex security controls. The guide names typical reasons to choose it: enterprise customers who require SAML, legacy identity providers that offer SAML but not OpenID Connect, compliance or procurement rules that mandate it, and existing SAML implementations that already work. It can also run alongside OIDC when a customer base needs both. The listed drawbacks are higher development complexity because of XML handling, limited native support in modern frameworks, difficulty for mobile and single-page applications, more manual customer onboarding than OIDC discovery, and greater long-term maintenance. Multi-tenant SaaS is workable but with added effort. The page gives no license requirements and refers readers to a separate article on the SAML single sign-on protocol.

semantic-index.title: Semantic indexing for Microsoft Copilot – Microsoft Learn
semantic-index.notes: Microsoft Copilot maps an organization's data into a lexical index and a semantic index built from content in Microsoft Graph. The semantic index is vector-based, so items with similar meaning sit close together, which lets search recognize word forms, synonyms and related content instead of only exact matches. It adds context to a prompt before the language model processes it, which improves relevance and grounding for answers in Microsoft 365 chat and apps. A tenant-level index covers text-based SharePoint Online files and shows results only to users who have permission, while a user-level index covers mailbox content and documents a person created, shared or is mentioned in. Copilot connectors can bring external data into the index. It is created for users with a paid Copilot license, every customer receives a tenant-level index, and admins do not need to switch it on or can turn it off. A site can be excluded by setting it not to appear in search results, which affects Microsoft Search as well. Delegated, shared and archived mailboxes and archived SharePoint data are not covered. Indexing does not change access rights, and prompts and responses are not used to train foundation models.

sharepoint-autofill-columns.title: Autofill columns overview – SharePoint – Microsoft Learn
sharepoint-autofill-columns.notes: Autofill columns in SharePoint use large language models to extract, summarize or generate content from files uploaded to a document library and store the result as metadata. A library owner writes a natural-language prompt about the document, and the answer fills a chosen column. Several prompts can be used, each tied to its own column, and extractive and generative prompts can be mixed. The stored values can be indexed, used in workflows or serve as criteria for information protection labels. Typical uses are classifying documents into a set of choices, pulling details such as education from resumes, or saving summaries. Availability is controlled by a tenant setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center, either for the whole tenant or for chosen sites, and only users with enough rights on the library can create or edit prompts. Limits include no support for person, location, image and lookup columns, no analysis of encrypted files, and no use on subsites or several system libraries. Changes to a document are picked up only when the file is reprocessed manually. Bulk processing of existing files was not yet available, and Microsoft notes that AI output can be wrong and should be checked.

sharepoint-global-navigation.title: SharePoint app bar and global navigation – Viva Connections – Microsoft Learn
sharepoint-global-navigation.notes: The SharePoint app bar is a bar on the left side of modern SharePoint sites and pages that gathers intranet resources together with personalized content such as sites, news, files and lists. Global navigation is the app bar tab that shows organizational resources, and it is the only tab that can be customized. Its aim is easier wayfinding across the intranet and quick access to key resources from anywhere in SharePoint. Admins can change the logo, set a title, and choose whether the links come from the home site navigation, hub navigation or site navigation. Audience targeting can be applied to menu links. A SharePoint home site is required, site owner permissions are needed to enable it, and viewers need at least read access to the home site. The Viva Connections icon appears only after a dashboard has been configured and published. Individual tabs cannot be turned off, the app bar cannot be disabled for specific sites, and it is unavailable on classic sites. External guests do not see it, and applying the extended header removes the site navigation. Changes can take from a few minutes up to a day to appear.

sharepoint-list-view-threshold.title: Items exceed the list view threshold – SharePoint Online – Microsoft Learn
sharepoint-list-view-threshold.notes: The list view threshold is a limit on how many items a SharePoint Online list may hold before views of that list are blocked. When the limit is exceeded, users see an error stating that the number of items exceeds the threshold and that tasks causing excessive server load, such as those involving all list items, are currently prohibited. SharePoint Online applies this through a feature called large list resource throttling. The default value is 5,000 items, and the message appears when the item count passes that defined limit while someone views the list in Microsoft 365. The troubleshooting article is short and gives no purpose beyond protecting the service from heavy operations on very large lists. It states no license requirements and no specific steps to fix the problem. Instead it points readers to a separate article about managing large lists and libraries in SharePoint, which contains recommendations and tips. The page does not say whether or how administrators can change the threshold.

sharepoint-managed-metadata.title: Introduction to managed metadata – SharePoint – Microsoft Learn
sharepoint-managed-metadata.notes: Managed metadata is the central administration of metadata in SharePoint, meaning information about information such as the title and author of a document. Its goals are consistent metadata use across sites, better findability through search, navigation based on metadata, and the ability to adjust terms as needs change. Terms are organized into term sets, which can be local to one site collection or global across sites that subscribe to a managed metadata service. Term sets can be closed, so users cannot add terms without permission, or open. Terms have a unique identifier and can carry several labels, including synonyms and multilingual ones. Managed terms are predefined, while enterprise keywords are free tags added by users that admins may later move into a term set. Groups act as security containers for term sets. The term store management tool is used to create and manage groups, term sets and terms. Managed metadata columns let users pick terms, and metadata navigation supports views and filters in lists and libraries. Global term sets need a SharePoint administrator or term store administrator. The page names no license requirements.

sign-in-frequency.title: Configure adaptive session lifetime policies – Conditional Access – Microsoft Learn
sign-in-frequency.notes: Sign-in frequency is a Conditional Access session control that sets how long a user can use a resource before being asked to sign in again. By default, Microsoft Entra ID uses a rolling window of 90 days and does not prompt again unless the security posture changes. Adaptive policies let admins shorten sessions for specific cases, such as unmanaged or shared devices, sensitive data reached from external networks, high-impact users and critical business apps. The time-based setting also applies to multifactor authentication. The every-time option requires full reauthentication whenever a session is evaluated and suits sensitive apps, privileged role activation, VPN access and risky users, while a strict variant in preview uses a very short validity window. Conditional Access needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, and other reauthentication settings, including remembering MFA on trusted devices, should be disabled first. Every-time without MFA can cause sign-in loops, and too many apps using it may tire users. Apps that set their own cookies may not honor the control, and browsers that persist cookies keep tokens valid until they expire.

solution-dependencies.title: Check for solution component dependencies – Power Platform – Microsoft Learn
solution-dependencies.notes: Solution component dependencies matter because a component cannot be deleted while another solution component has a published dependency on it. A managed solution likewise cannot be uninstalled if one of its components is used in a customization of another unmanaged solution. The article is aimed at developers and shows how to read dependency data with code, for example to check before a delete or an uninstall. Four messages are described, each available as a .NET SDK request and as a Web API function. RetrieveDependentComponents returns the components that directly depend on a given component, such as the attributes that reference a global option set, or the attributes, views and forms of an entity. RetrieveRequiredComponents does the reverse and returns the components a given component directly depends on. RetrieveDependenciesForDelete lists dependencies that could block deleting a component, and RetrieveDependenciesForUninstall lists those that could block uninstalling a managed solution. The page names no license or permission requirements and no explicit limits. It points to the SDK and Web API references for the exact structure of the results.

supplier-communications-agent.title: Supplier Communications Agent overview – Supply Chain Management – Microsoft Learn
supplier-communications-agent.notes: The Supplier Communications Agent is an AI-based agent in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management that automates many communications with vendors. It is a production-ready preview feature that falls under supplemental terms of use, and its documentation is prerelease and may change. The aim is to cut manual, repetitive procurement work such as vendor follow-ups and purchase order changes so purchasers can focus on more complex tasks. One function is purchase order follow-up, where the agent generates emails asking vendors to confirm an order or explain a late delivery. These emails can be sent immediately or saved as drafts for a person to review first. The second function is processing of purchase order communication: Copilot reads emails from some or all vendors, works out the subject, such as a confirmation or a change request, and identifies the related purchase order numbers. It then matches the extracted details to system fields and proposes changes that purchasers can review and apply without opening each order. Usage incurs charges tied to Microsoft Copilot Studio messages. The page does not state licenses, prerequisites, quotas or how accurate the extracted data is.

sysmon.title: Sysmon – Sysinternals – Microsoft Learn
sysmon.notes: Sysmon, short for System Monitor, is a Windows system service and device driver that stays active across reboots after installation and writes system activity to the Windows event log. Its events can be collected with Windows Event Collection or SIEM agents and analyzed to spot malicious or unusual behavior and to understand how intruders and malware operate in a network. Sysmon logs process creation with full command lines, including the parent process, and records hashes of process images using algorithms such as SHA1, MD5, SHA256 or IMPHASH. Process and session GUIDs help correlate events even when Windows reuses process IDs. It also records driver and DLL loading, raw disk reads, optional network connections, file creation time changes, named pipes, WMI activity and DNS queries. A configuration file with include and exclude rules filters events per type and is reloaded when the registry changes. It runs on current Windows client and server versions, and the license must be accepted at install. Sysmon does not analyze events itself and does not hide from attackers. Network logging is off by default, and enabling image load events can create very large log volumes.

teams-call-queues.title: Create a Teams call queue – Microsoft Teams – Microsoft Learn
teams-call-queues.notes: A call queue in Microsoft Teams distributes incoming calls among representatives and can provide a greeting, music while callers wait, call redirection and further handling. Admins create one in the Teams admin center under Voice, using either a quick setup for simple routing or an advanced setup for complex needs, or they use PowerShell cmdlets. Settings include the language for text-to-speech prompts, a greeting as audio file or text, hold music, and a routing method of attendant, serial, round robin or longest idle. Presence-based routing sends calls only to agents who are available. Callback can be offered to eligible callers, and exception handling covers overflow, timeout and no available agents, each ending in disconnect or a transfer to a person, voice app, external number or voicemail. Templates add automatic or compliance recording. A queue that answers calls directly needs a resource account with the Teams Phone resource account license, and a number if caller ID features are used. Limits apply to the number of members, authorized users, queued calls and wait time. Group changes can take hours before the first call arrives, and channel-based queues work only on Windows and Mac clients.

teams-calling-plans.title: Calling Plans for Microsoft Teams – Microsoft Learn
teams-calling-plans.notes: Calling Plans give Teams Phone a connection to the public telephone network so users can place and receive external calls, and the page calls this the simplest way to link Teams Phone to the PSTN. There are three options: a domestic plan for calls within a country, an international plan that adds calls abroad, and a pay-as-you-go plan billed by usage. Domestic and international plans include minutes, while incoming calls are included without limit in all three. Users in the same country on the same plan share a pooled set of minutes, and calls beyond the pool are charged per minute. The country is set by the location of the user's license, not by the billing address. A Teams Phone add-on license must be bought first, followed by the calling plan, or a bundle can be used, and plans are assigned per user in the Microsoft 365 admin center. A know-your-customer check may be needed before numbers are acquired or ported. Pay-as-you-go users cannot make outgoing calls until the plan is funded, through post-usage billing or communication credits depending on the agreement type. Availability varies by country, and the page gives no prices.

teams-certified-devices.title: Microsoft Teams certified devices – Microsoft Learn
teams-certified-devices.notes: The Microsoft Teams device certification program tests personal and shared devices against specifications so that they meet expectations for quality, reliability and compatibility and give users a better meeting experience with Teams. The tests cover areas such as audio and video quality, the user interface, device management and security. Only devices that pass all certification requirements and the related tests may carry the designation Certified for Microsoft Teams. The page groups devices into categories: Teams Rooms on Windows, Teams Rooms on Android, certified Teams panels, certified Teams phones, certified Teams displays and certified personal devices. IP phones appear only as part of the phones category, and their details are on a separate page rather than here. The page also points to a certification overview, partner device certification, and the supported Windows and Android versions for Teams Rooms. It does not describe licensing needs, typical deployment scenarios, individual models or limits of the program.

teams-meeting-lifecycle-events.title: Get change notifications for Teams meeting call events – Microsoft Graph – Microsoft Learn
teams-meeting-lifecycle-events.notes: Microsoft Graph change notifications let an app subscribe to call events of Teams online meetings, namely a call starting, a call ending and roster updates. The subscription targets the meeting call events resource of a specific online meeting, identified by its URL-encoded join web URL. Roster updates report participants joining or leaving the call or the lobby, and the participants delta shows who changed, with a removed state marking people who left and a lobby flag showing who is waiting. Notifications can be rich, carrying encrypted resource data so no extra call is needed, or basic, containing only the resource ID. Since no API retrieves meeting call data by that ID, the page recommends rich notifications, which need a certificate for encryption and decryption of the payload. Only application permissions work, specifically reading or reading and writing all online meetings, and delegated permissions are not supported. The feature exists in both the beta and v1.0 endpoints. A subscription lasts at most three days and must be renewed or recreated for longer monitoring. The page states no license requirements.

teams-message-extensions.title: Message extensions overview – Microsoft Teams – Microsoft Learn
teams-message-extensions.notes: Message extensions let users interact with a web service from buttons and forms in the Teams client, either to search or to start an action in an external system. They can be invoked from the compose area, the command bar or directly from a message, and results can come back as formatted cards. Typical examples are booking a resource, finding an Azure DevOps work item to share as an adaptive card, and creating and assigning a bug in a ticket system. Each app manifest holds one message extension with a limited number of commands, and each command is either an action or a search type. Action commands open a modal dialog for collecting or showing information, while search commands return a list of cards from a typed term or a pasted link and cannot be started from a message. Link unfurling turns a pasted URL from a subscribed domain into a detailed card, but works only for bot-based extensions. Extensions can be built agent-based with the Teams SDK, which needs a registered bot, or API-based from an OpenAPI description, which supports search but not action commands or link unfurling. They cannot be addressed by @ mention in the compose box. The page names no license requirements.

teamsfx.title: TeamsFx SDK – Microsoft Teams developer – Microsoft Learn
teamsfx.notes: TeamsFx is a software development kit that lowers the effort of adding Teams single sign-on and of reaching cloud resources, using short code lines without extra configuration. It works in browser and Node.js environments and supports user authentication for a Teams tab, a Teams bot and an Azure Function. The page is archived: Microsoft no longer supports the kit for Microsoft 365 Copilot extensions, Microsoft 365 agents or modern Teams app scenarios, and it receives only community support on GitHub for a limited time. New projects should not use it, and existing solutions are advised to migrate to the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK or, for plain Teams apps and bots, the Teams SDK. Components include credential classes for user identity in the browser, user identity in Node.js through on-behalf-of exchange, and app identity for jobs without a user. There is a prompt for bot single sign-on, helpers for Microsoft Graph and SQL access, and API clients with several authentication providers. Logging is off by default. Prerequisites listed are Visual Studio Code, the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit, Node.js, Teams and a supported browser. Several elements, such as the TeamsFx class, are deprecated, and admin consent may be needed.
